notes: The test maps the standard MIM conditional HLAboolean attribute, the public Enable/Disable Time Constrained services, the timeConstrainedEnabled callback, and public MIM request/subscription/reflection APIs. It obtains the initial state from the standard MOM rather than assuming a default. Installed-package results are bounded provider evidence only, not proof of provider-independent behavior or conformance.

requirements.statement: The standard MIM declares HLAtimeConstrained as a conditional HLAboolean updated whenever Enable Time Constrained or Disable Time Constrained succeeds. HLAboolean is represented by HLAinteger32BE with HLAfalse=0 and HLAtrue=1. The scenario reads the starting state from the MIM, checks one conditional value after each opposite-state operation, and restores the observed starting state.
When the observed MIM value is false, the subject invokes Enable Time Constrained and the monitor checks the conditional HLAtrue value; the test does not assume the initial state is false.

After a successful Enable Time Constrained invocation, the subject services callbacks until exactly one timeConstrainedEnabled callback is observed. The test allows the standard callback to be delivered asynchronously and does not require one on disable.
When the observed MIM value is true, the subject invokes Disable Time Constrained and the monitor checks the conditional HLAfalse value; the test then restores the previously observed state.
The monitor directly requests the standard HLAtimeConstrained value before and after each successful service transition and checks it against the transition target.
The monitor subscribes to the standard HLAfederate MOM object's HLAfederateHandle and HLAtimeConstrained attributes to identify the subject object and receive its conditional updates.

The monitor validates exactly one conditional reflection for each successful transition, including the HLAboolean value, reliable transport, empty tag, invalid producer handle, and absent DDM-region metadata.
